title: customer-lambda-incident-timeline-draft-ryan-lee
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for internal timeline, commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses and a short draft to send to the customer.

Summary (short): Customer LAMBDA observed elevated 504 gateway timeouts and degraded throughput during batch inference on 2025-11-01 22:00 UTC. Root cause unknown; initial signal points to intermittent KV-cache OOM + model shard load contention on Dedicated pool 'ded-lambda-01'.

Timeline (local timestamps UTC):
- 2025-11-01 21:45  -  Customer reported higher tail latency (~>2s) and occasional 504s via customer-monitoring alert (JIRA-INC-4123). First Slack ping from CS: "customer seeing 504s on production, affects /v1/chat generate route".
- 2025-11-01 21:50  -  I (Ryan) pulled basic metrics from Console: Token QPS normal but tail latency P99 spiked from 180ms -> 2.2s. Error rate for route /v1/chat: 0.8% 504s.
- 2025-11-01 21:55  -  Ran quick health checks on ded-lambda-01 nodes (internal):
  - curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://ded-lambda-01.internal/api/v1/health -> 200 OK
  - kubectl top pods -n ded-lambda | grep lambda -> CPU OK, memory on model-worker-2 at 92%
- 2025-11-01 22:05  -  Collected logs from model-worker-2 (kubectl logs -n ded-lambda model-worker-2):
  - repeated lines: "[warn] KV cache nearing capacity: entries=987641, limit=1M"
  - at 22:03:14: "ERROR model_shard_loader.cc:142] failed to allocate shard: cudamalloc returned out of memory"
  - at 22:03:16: "[error] request id=abcd1234 failed: downstream timeout forwarding to model-worker"
- 2025-11-01 22:10  -  Observed a GRPC error in the proxy logs when forwarding large chat requests:
  - "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (size=5242881)"
- 2025-11-01 22:18  -  Attempted restart of model-worker-2 (rolling restart): kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-worker -n ded-lambda -> restart completed, node returned to service 22:24
- 2025-11-01 22:30  -  Errors reduced briefly then returned. Traces show increased cache misses after restart; model-worker-1 became hotspot (CPU > 90%).
- 2025-11-01 23:00  -  Gathered heap/kvcache stats via /metrics endpoint:
  - kvcache_entries_total{node="model-worker-2"} 1001000
  - kvcache_misses_total surged by 8x at 22:04
  - eviction_rate jumped after restart (22:25)
- 2025-11-02 02:10  -  Customer reports continued sporadic 504s under burst traffic.

Commands & outputs tried (raw snippets):
- curl to /v1/chat with a synthetic long context to reproduce:
  curl -X POST https://ded-lambda-01.internal/v1/chat \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long prompt repeated 4k tokens>"}]}'
  -> proxy returned 504 after 15s. Proxy log: "upstream timed out (110)"

- kubectl logs model-worker-2 -n ded-lambda | tail -n 50:
  [warn] KV cache nearing capacity: entries=987641, limit=1000000
  ERROR model_shard_loader.cc:142] failed to allocate shard: cudamalloc returned out of memory
  [info] evicting 512 entries to make room

- redis-cli -h kvcache-ded-lambda get stats -> shows high used_memory and lots of evictions

- docker exec -it model-worker-2 /bin/bash; cat /proc/meminfo -> shows high GPU mem usage and kernel OOM logs correlate with 22:03

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache growth + insufficient eviction/backpressure -> causes model-worker to OOM when attempting large shard allocations under bursty requests. Evidence: kvcache entries ~1M (at limit), OOM error in model_shard_loader, eviction spikes after restart.
2) Large single-request payloads exceeding GRPC message size leading to proxy errors and perceived 504s. Evidence: grpc error "received message larger than max" in proxy at 22:10. We saw synthetic long context reproduce 504.
3) Hotspotting due to uneven request routing -> model-worker-1 becomes CPU hotspot after model-worker-2 restart. Evidence: CPU spikes and elevated misses on worker-1. May be related to sticky routing/cache affinity loss after restart.
4) Underlying driver/kernel issue causing intermittent cudamalloc failures under memory pressure. Evidence: cudamalloc OOM lines; need GPU driver logs to confirm.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolling restart of model-worker-2 (22:18) to clear transient memory fragmentation  -  reduced errors briefly.
- Increased KV cache eviction aggressiveness for ded-lambda pool as a temporary knob (applied 23:05): set kvcache.eviction_threshold=0.85 via feature-flag.
- Added a proxy rule to reject requests larger than 5MB with 413 to avoid grpc large-message path (change staged; to be enabled after tests).

Data still wanted / next steps:
- Collect GPU driver logs from model-worker-2 for 22:00-22:06 window (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q)  -  owned by infra/SRE (Evelyn P).
- Export full model-worker memory allocation traces (malloc backtraces) if available.
- Confirm routing table during restart window (was there a surge to worker-1?)  -  ask infra to provide haproxy/proxy metrics.
- Reproduce high-load scenario in staging with similar KV cache size and long-context requests to see if cudamalloc OOM is reproducible.
- Evaluate increasing kvcache capacity + proactive eviction vs backpressure on request acceptance.

Internal draft to send to customer (short, internal tone  -  we will refine before sending):
--- DRAFT ---
Subject: Follow-up: Elevated 504s on /v1/chat (Incident JIRA-INC-4123)
Hi <Customer Ops>,
We investigated the tail-latency spikes you reported on 2025-11-01. Initial root cause appears to be memory pressure on one of the dedicated inference nodes (ded-lambda-01) where the KV cache grew to capacity and the model shard loader hit GPU allocation failures. This caused the request proxy to timeout when forwarding larger chat requests.
What we did so far:
- Restarted the affected worker and applied a temporary more-aggressive KV eviction threshold.
- Staged a proxy guard to reject oversized requests to prevent grpc large-message failures.
- Collected logs and traces; we're working with infra to pull GPU driver logs and allocation traces.
Next steps we will take and ETA:
- Validate root cause with GPU driver logs and reproduce in staging (ETA 24 hours).
- If confirmed, propose one of: (a) increase KV cache capacity for your Dedicated pool, (b) enable request-size backpressure to refuse very large contexts, or (c) apply model sharding adjustments to lower per-node memory peaks.
We’ll send a follow-up with findings and recommended remediation by EOD tomorrow.
Thanks for the patience  -  we know this impacts your users and we prioritize stabilizing your production traffic.
Best,
Ryan (CS)
--- end draft ---

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Get GPU logs (Evelyn) + confirm driver version.
- Ask infra to temporarily route small percentage (5%) of traffic to an isolated pool to see if errors persist.
- Add a synthetic test in load-tests repo that simulates long-context chat with kvcache pre-warm to 1M entries. (PR idea: github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/pull/xx)
- Consider a short-term customer config: hard limit of 4k tokens per request on the Dedicated pool and rate-limit large-batch endpoints.

Unresolved questions:
- Was there any concurrent model reload/rolling update around 22:00 that could have increased memory pressure? (check release-engineering deploy logs)
- Why did eviction not keep pace earlier  -  is eviction_threshold or policy misconfigured for this pool?

If I don't respond in Slack, page me (pager id in Ops rota) or look at JIRA-INC-4123 for latest notes.

End of scratchpad.
